knowledge.doc: Scans an array of 0xC-byte entries starting at `ent`, looking for one whose flags byte has bit 0x20 set and whose id field (u16 at offset 6) equals `want`. Records the (adjusted) scan index of the match, or leaves it 0, at *idxOut, and returns a pointer to the matching entry (or NULL if none matched). The scan processes entries until (and including) the one whose flags byte has bit 0x80 set (a "last entry" sentinel). After the scan, the value stored at *idxOut is reduced by half of the total entry count scanned (rounded down towards zero), giving a signed/relative index rather than an absolute one.

knowledge.doc: Registers a VRAM "tile cache" slot. cellIdx = (a1-0x7000)>>6 decodes a vram-offset argument (a1, e.g. 0x7A40/0x79C0 at call sites) into a 64-cell grid index. Unless a3&1 suppresses it, builds a local RECT (x/y from cellIdx/a1 low bits, w = a2<<4, h=1) and calls LoadImage(&rect, (void*)a0) to DMA a one-row strip into VRAM. Unless a3&2 suppresses it, packs (a0 & 0xFFFFFF) | (a2<<24) into D_80082EC0[cellIdx] (source-address/tile-set-id cache entry). If cellIdx is one of the first 64 slots and a2>=0x11, clears the paired "loaded" flag at D_80082EC0[cellIdx+0x40]. Confirmed sibling: src/w_800483AC.c already calls this as func_8003F80C((s32)buf, 0x7A40, 1, 2) etc., consistent with this signature/semantics.

knowledge.doc: Bump/ring allocator (confirmed by config/knowledge/func_800483AC.json's caller doc: called with 0x2000, returns scratch buffer pointer). Returns the current write pointer (D_80081480) and advances it by `size` bytes. If the advanced pointer would reach/pass the end of the buffer (base D_8008148C + total size D_80080A7C), the write pointer is reset back to the buffer base and the GPU is synced via DrawSync(0) before the (now possibly-reset) pointer is returned and advanced. This function's TU is compiled -G0 (small-data disabled) -- same TU family as code5.c/w_8004878C.c which touch these same 3 globals as plain s32 scalars; -G0 makes gcc emit fully independent lui/%hi+lw/sw/%lo pairs per access (no materialised/reused base register), unlike the default -G8 TU siblings (func_80041AB0/func_80043CD0) that force hi/lo via an oversized-struct-with-padding trick on the SAME symbols. Declaring these as plain s32 (not the padded struct) was required to reproduce the fresh-lui-per-access pattern; a struct/volatile-struct attempt kept materialising a shared base address register across accesses and did not match. Comparison operand order in the C (`base+D_80080A7C <= D_80081480+size` rather than the mirrored `>=`) was needed to get v0/v1 register assignment to match retail's evaluation order.

knowledge.doc: Draws a two-byte-code (Shift-JIS-ish) string as font-tile blits at a PS1 GPU level. For each 2-byte code read from arg0: builds code=(hi<<8)|lo, advances the source pointer by 2, then classifies code into a tile index via a small range/equality table (0x8140 -> 0, two ~0x1A-wide contiguous ranges and one ~0xA-wide range map through code+0x7DC0/0x7DC1, plus literal 0x8144->0xE and 0x817C->0xD); anything else clears the draw flag (glyph is skipped, pen still advances). When the flag is set, computes source tile (x,y) from the index (tile_x = (index&7)*3+0x340, tile_y = (index>>3)<<4, fixed w=3,h=0x10), StoreImage's it into a scratch buffer, LoadImage's it back at (arg1_pen, arg2), calls DrawSync(0), then advances the pen by 3 and loops until the next code byte is 0.

If prev is null, the node was the list head, so the global head pointer D_80081498 is updated to the node's next, and next->prev is cleared. Finally both next/prev pointers on the node are zeroed.

knowledge.doc: Converts a 32-bit value whose 4-bit nibbles each hold a decimal digit (0-9) into the equivalent base-10 integer: for i=0..7, extracts nibble i (mask 0xF<<(4i)), multiplies by pow10=10^i while still shifted into position, then arithmetic-shifts the 32-bit truncated product back down by 4i and accumulates. Net effect (assuming valid BCD-like input) is sum = Σ digit_i * 10^i.

knowledge.doc: Registers a VRAM "tile cache" slot. cellIdx = (a1-0x7000)>>6 decodes a vram-offset argument (a1, e.g. 0x7A40/0x79C0 at call sites) into a 64-cell grid index. Unless a3&1 suppresses it, builds a local RECT (x/y from cellIdx/a1 low bits, w = a2<<4, h=1) and calls LoadImage(&rect, (void*)a0) to DMA a one-row strip into VRAM. Unless a3&2 suppresses it, packs (a0 & 0xFFFFFF) | (a2<<24) into D_80082EC0[cellIdx] (source-address/tile-set-id cache entry). If cellIdx is one of the first 64 slots and a2>=0x11, clears the paired "loaded" flag at D_80082EC0[cellIdx+0x40]. Confirmed sibling: src/w_800483AC.c already calls this as func_8003F80C((s32)buf, 0x7A40, 1, 2) etc., consistent with this signature/semantics.

knowledge.doc: Registers a VRAM "tile cache" slot. cellIdx = (a1-0x7000)>>6 decodes a vram-offset argument (a1, e.g. 0x7A40/0x79C0 at call sites) into a 64-cell grid index. Unless a3&1 suppresses it, builds a local RECT (x/y from cellIdx/a1 low bits, w = a2<<4, h=1) and calls LoadImage(&rect, (void*)a0) to DMA a one-row strip into VRAM. Unless a3&2 suppresses it, packs (a0 & 0xFFFFFF) | (a2<<24) into D_80082EC0[cellIdx] (source-address/tile-set-id cache entry). If cellIdx is one of the first 64 slots and a2>=0x11, clears the paired "loaded" flag at D_80082EC0[cellIdx+0x40]. Confirmed sibling: src/w_800483AC.c already calls this as func_8003F80C((s32)buf, 0x7A40, 1, 2) etc., consistent with this signature/semantics.

knowledge.doc: Bump/ring allocator (confirmed by config/knowledge/func_800483AC.json's caller doc: called with 0x2000, returns scratch buffer pointer). Returns the current write pointer (D_80081480) and advances it by `size` bytes. If the advanced pointer would reach/pass the end of the buffer (base D_8008148C + total size D_80080A7C), the write pointer is reset back to the buffer base and the GPU is synced via DrawSync(0) before the (now possibly-reset) pointer is returned and advanced. This function's TU is compiled -G0 (small-data disabled) -- same TU family as code5.c/w_8004878C.c which touch these same 3 globals as plain s32 scalars; -G0 makes gcc emit fully independent lui/%hi+lw/sw/%lo pairs per access (no materialised/reused base register), unlike the default -G8 TU siblings (func_80041AB0/func_80043CD0) that force hi/lo via an oversized-struct-with-padding trick on the SAME symbols. Declaring these as plain s32 (not the padded struct) was required to reproduce the fresh-lui-per-access pattern; a struct/volatile-struct attempt kept materialising a shared base address register across accesses and did not match. Comparison operand order in the C (`base+D_80080A7C <= D_80081480+size` rather than the mirrored `>=`) was needed to get v0/v1 register assignment to match retail's evaluation order.

knowledge.doc: Draws a two-byte-code (Shift-JIS-ish) string as font-tile blits at a PS1 GPU level. For each 2-byte code read from arg0: builds code=(hi<<8)|lo, advances the source pointer by 2, then classifies code into a tile index via a small range/equality table (0x8140 -> 0, two ~0x1A-wide contiguous ranges and one ~0xA-wide range map through code+0x7DC0/0x7DC1, plus literal 0x8144->0xE and 0x817C->0xD); anything else clears the draw flag (glyph is skipped, pen still advances). When the flag is set, computes source tile (x,y) from the index (tile_x = (index&7)*3+0x340, tile_y = (index>>3)<<4, fixed w=3,h=0x10), StoreImage's it into a scratch buffer, LoadImage's it back at (arg1_pen, arg2), calls DrawSync(0), then advances the pen by 3 and loops until the next code byte is 0.
calls: StoreImage(RECT *rect, void *p) - copies a tile-sized region out of the font sheet into a scratch VRAM/buf staging area
LoadImage(RECT *rect, void *p) - loads the staged tile back in at the destination (x, dest_y) position
DrawSync(s32 mode) - DrawSync(0), waits for the GPU transfer to finish before the next glyph
